::: {.kicker}
Specimen
:::

This page exists to be looked at rather than read. Every setting the sheet
makes a claim about is exercised somewhere below, so that the claims can be
checked instead of believed. If a rule here renders wrong, the rule is wrong.

The paragraph you are reading is the text stream: Source Serif 4 at whatever
size satisfies a 62-character measure, leaded at 1.45, with `text-wrap: pretty`
doing what it can about ladders. This second paragraph is a continuation, so it
is indented one and a half ems and gives up its leading in exchange -- the book
setting, not the web one.

## Real small caps, not shrunken capitals

This heading is set in genuine `smcp` glyphs drawn at small-caps proportions,
not capitals scaled down.[^synth] The difference is in the stroke weight: a
scaled capital goes thin next to lowercase, and a real small cap does not.
Compare a line of each: <span style="font-variant-caps: small-caps">handgloves
in small caps</span> against <span style="font-variant-caps: none;
font-size: 0.72em; text-transform: uppercase">handgloves faked by scaling</span>.

[^synth]: The sheet sets `font-synthesis: none`, so if the webfont fails to
load nothing is faked -- the fallback simply has no small caps. That is the
intended failure: absent, not counterfeit.

## Old-style figures in text, lining figures in tables

In running text the figures are old-style and proportional, so 1848, 1972 and
2026 sit in the line like lowercase letters rather than standing above it. The
same numerals in a table go tabular and lining, because columns have to align:

| Cut      | Optical size | Glyphs | Bytes  |
|----------|--------------|--------|--------|
| Roman    | 8–60         | 550    | 191268 |
| Italic   | 8–60         | 436    | 152312 |
| Caption  | 8            | 550    | 0      |
| Display  | 60           | 550    | 0      |

## Optical sizing is doing something

The display line at the top of this page and the body text you are reading are
the same font file at different points on the `opsz` axis. The display cut has
finer hairlines and tighter spacing; the text cut is sturdier. Set
`font-optical-sizing: none` in the inspector and the headline will visibly
coarsen.

## Word-sized graphics

Sparklines belong inside the sentence, at the size and colour of the sentence.
Render times fell over the last eight builds
<svg class="spark" viewBox="0 0 48 12" aria-label="sparkline showing a decline"><polyline points="0,2 6,3 12,3 18,5 24,5 30,7 36,8 42,8 48,10"/></svg>
and the cache hit rate went the other way
<svg class="spark" viewBox="0 0 48 12" aria-label="sparkline showing a rise"><polyline points="0,10 6,9 12,8 18,8 24,6 30,5 36,4 42,2 48,1"/></svg>.
They inherit `currentColor` and `1em`, take no frame, and are never wrapped in
a figure.

## Three registers

Display, caption small caps, folio -- a 1.5 step apart, with no fourth. The
kicker at the top of this page is folio with 0.28em of tracking; this heading
is caption; the title is display. Body text and sidenotes are not registers,
they are the text stream at 1em and 0.82em.[^registers]

[^registers]: Which is the honest reading of "exactly three ramps": three
*labelling* ramps. Counting the reading sizes as ramps would make it five, and
counting them as forbidden would leave the sidenotes at body size.

The only accent on the site is spent on [links](https://joehalliwell.com), and
nowhere else. Everything else separating one thing from another is size,
tracking, or how far the ink has been mixed toward the paper.
